title: the Panchadashi (selections)
tomorrow: a painted scene on a starched cloth. where did the cloth go?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Panchadashi opened with the senses: sounds change, the knowing of them neither rises nor sets. Today, two fathers, and a message that changes everything without changing anything.

A screenshot goes around saying someone got fired. It isn't true. They spend the night sick about it anyway. The Panchadashi tells an older version. A son has gone abroad. A traveler brings his father news: your son has died. The father weeps. But the report was false; the son is alive and well. Meanwhile another father's son really has died far away, and someone tells him the boy is doing fine. That father goes about his day untroubled. So what, exactly, made the first man grieve?
screen: `A FALSE SCREENSHOT, A REAL NIGHT.` → `TWO FATHERS, TWO REPORTS.` → `WHAT MADE HIM GRIEVE?`

segments.voice: The chapter draws a line between two kinds of making. There's the world as Ishvara, the Lord, makes it: the son himself, the road, the far country. And there's the world each person builds on top of it in the mind: my son, gone; my son, safe. The grief came from the picture the father was holding, not from the son. A second example: one gem on a table. One person who gets it is delighted, one who loses it is crushed, a third hardly notices. The gem doesn't change. The minds around it do. So bondage lives in that second world, the one the mind makes. It doesn't ask anyone to pretend the outer world isn't there; a real son still matters. And seeing the layer clearly is a step toward knowing the self from yesterday, the awareness under all of it. Now the week, in one breath. A father who says look again. A line that reads both ways. A text that points instead of commanding. The boundless, met in the heart. One clay in every pot. Sounds that change around a knowing that doesn't. And a father's tears over a picture.
screen: `THE WORLD AS IT'S GIVEN.` · `THE WORLD THE MIND LAYS OVER IT.` · `ONE GEM, THREE REACTIONS.` · then, large: `THE GRIEF WAS IN THE PICTURE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let one small worry about something that hasn't happened come to mind. Notice the picture the mind has built around it, the faces, the words, the ending. Then let the picture be just a picture, and come back to the breath, which is happening right now.
The Panchadashi: a book of Advaita verses. Here, it splits the world as it's given from the world the mind lays on top.
Keep this one: the Panchadashi, selections, where the grief was in the picture. That's a week of knowing.

howItsDone: In Advaita Vedanta, teachers use the Panchadashi's two fathers to show students the difference between the world as given and the world the mind builds, as a step toward self-knowledge.

fork.setup: one gem sits on a table. one person gets it and is delighted; one loses it and is crushed; one hardly notices. what changed?
options: only the minds around it; the gem is the same.
the gem's value went up and down with each owner.
nothing at all; all three feel the same inside.
fork.reveal: The Panchadashi's point: the gem doesn't change. The world each mind builds around it does, and that's where the joy and the grief live.

original.note: Sanskrit Ishvara, the Lord; in this chapter, the maker of the world as it's given, apart from the mind's own layer.

chat.meaning: The first father wept over a false report; his grief came from the picture he held. The Panchadashi locates bondage in the world the mind builds.
